pointers.sentence: Its module's docstring says in capitals what the view is not for: its views and functions "are only to be used during development, and SHOULD NOT be used in a production setting" (`django/views/static.py`).

The reference gives the reason, that the view "is not hardened for production use" (`docs/ref/views.txt`), and the static files app's documentation says of that app's view, which ends in this one, that it is "grossly inefficient and probably insecure" (`docs/ref/contrib/staticfiles.txt`).

The reference gives the reason, that the view "is not hardened for production use" (`docs/ref/views.txt`), and the static files app's documentation says of that app's view, which ends in this one, that it is "grossly inefficient and probably insecure" (`docs/ref/contrib/staticfiles.txt`).

The view is an ordinary function with an ordinary signature: the request, a path, and two options that a URLconf passes as extra arguments, `"document_root"` and `"show_indexes"` (`django/views/static.py:serve`).
A path that would climb out makes it raise `SuspiciousFileOperation`, a `SuspiciousOperation`, which `response_for_exception` answers with a 400 (`django/utils/_os.py:safe_join`).

Under `settings.DEBUG`, which is when `django.conf.urls.static.static` routes a prefix to the view at all, that 400 is the debug page that `technical_500_response` makes ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md#which-exception-becomes-which-response)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
Nothing checks for a missing document root: the parameter defaults to `None`, and `safe_join` hands it to `os.path.join`, which raises the `TypeError` (`django/utils/_os.py:safe_join`).
The file's time is cut to whole seconds before it is compared with the header's, which `parse_http_date` returns as whole seconds (`django/views/static.py:was_modified_since`).

`directory_index` looks for a template named `"static/directory_index.html"` or, failing that, `"static/directory_index"` among the project's own, and when there is neither it reads the one in `django/views/templates/` and renders it with an engine made for the occasion.
The list leaves out every name that begins with a dot, and marks directories with a slash (`django/views/static.py:directory_index`).

The index of the document root leaves out the file named `".proofs"`, and each index holds `"../"`, the built-in template's own link to the directory above (`django/views/templates/directory_index.html`).
**`static()`** is a helper for a URLconf, in `django/conf/urls/static.py`.

For any other it returns an empty list when `settings.DEBUG` is off, or when the prefix has a host in it, so the same URLconf can be deployed and simply has no such pattern in production (`django/conf/urls/static.py:static`).

Django's test runner turns `settings.DEBUG` off for the tests, whatever the settings module says, unless it is run with `--debug-mode`, and its system checks import the root URLconf before the first test runs; so a test that turns it on again with `override_settings` finds no pattern under the prefix (`django/conf/urls/static.py:static`, `django/test/utils.py:setup_test_environment`, `django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.run_tests`).

**The static files app** has a view of its own, `django.contrib.staticfiles.views.serve`, which finds the file with the app's finders and calls this one with the file's directory as the document root (`django/contrib/staticfiles/views.py:serve`).

**The test framework** uses the view the same way for a live server: its handlers for static and media files call `serve` directly with a directory of their own (`django/test/testcases.py:FSFilesHandler.serve`, [A server in a thread: `LiveServerTestCase`](../testing/live-server.md)).
